definition: An object that produces a magnetic field and attracts magnetic materials such as iron, steel, nickel, and cobalt.
clues: This is an object that produces a magnetic field
It attracts certain materials
Iron and steel are attracted to it
An object with a magnetic field — attracts iron, steel, nickel and cobalt; has a north and south pole

definition: A magnet that produces its own magnetic field all the time and does not need an external field to maintain it. Made from hard magnetic materials such as steel.
clues: This is a type of magnet
It maintains its magnetism without an external field
Steel is used to make this type
A magnet that retains its magnetism permanently — made from hard magnetic materials like steel; does not lose its field when removed from another magnet

definition: A material that becomes a magnet only when placed in an external magnetic field. Made from soft magnetic materials such as iron. Loses its magnetism when the external field is removed.
clues: This is a type of magnet
It only becomes magnetic in the presence of another magnet
Iron is used to make this type
A soft magnetic material (like iron) that becomes magnetised in an external field — loses its magnetism when the external field is removed

definition: The region around a magnet where a magnetic force is experienced. Represented by field lines that go from north to south pole outside the magnet.
clues: This is a region in space around a magnet
Magnetic forces are experienced within it
It is represented by lines that go from north to south
The region around a magnet where forces act on magnetic materials — represented by field lines running from north to south outside the magnet

definition: A line used to represent a magnetic field. The direction of the line shows the direction of the force on a north pole. Lines are closer together where the field is stronger.
clues: This is used to represent a magnetic field
Its direction shows the force on a north pole
Closer lines indicate a stronger field
Lines showing the direction and strength of a magnetic field — closer together = stronger field; direction shows force on a north pole

definition: The end of a magnet from which magnetic field lines emerge. Like poles repel; unlike poles attract — a north pole is attracted to a south pole.
clues: This is a feature of a magnet
Field lines emerge from it
It is attracted to the opposite type of pole
The pole from which magnetic field lines emerge — it is attracted to a south pole and repelled by another north pole

definition: The end of a magnet into which magnetic field lines enter. Attracted to a north pole; repelled by another south pole.
clues: This is a feature of a magnet
Field lines enter it
It is attracted to the opposite type of pole
The pole into which magnetic field lines enter — attracted to a north pole, repelled by another south pole

definition: The force between unlike magnetic poles (north and south) or between a magnet and a magnetic material, pulling them together.
clues: This is a type of magnetic force
It acts between unlike poles
Unlike poles pull towards each other
The pulling force between a north and south pole, or between a magnet and a magnetic material — unlike poles attract

definition: The force between like magnetic poles (north-north or south-south) pushing them apart.
clues: This is a type of magnetic force
It acts between like poles
Like poles push away from each other
The pushing force between two north poles or two south poles — like poles repel each other

definition: A material that can be attracted by a magnet. Magnetic materials include iron, steel, nickel, and cobalt.
clues: This is a type of material
It is attracted by a magnet
Iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are examples
A material that is attracted to a magnet — only iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are magnetic; aluminium and copper are not

definition: A device containing a small, freely rotating magnet (needle) that aligns itself with the Earth's magnetic field, pointing towards magnetic north.
clues: This is a device used for navigation
It contains a small freely rotating magnet
It aligns with Earth's magnetic field
A navigational tool with a freely pivoting magnetic needle — it aligns with Earth's magnetic field and points towards magnetic north

definition: The magnetic field surrounding the Earth, produced by electric currents in the Earth's liquid iron core. It acts like a giant bar magnet with poles near the geographic poles.
clues: This is a magnetic field surrounding a planet
It is produced by currents in the liquid iron core
It protects Earth from solar wind
A global magnetic field produced by convection currents in Earth's liquid iron core — it deflects charged particles from the Sun

definition: The magnetic effect produced by an electric current. When current flows through a wire, it creates a magnetic field around the wire.
clues: This is the link between electricity and magnetism
An electric current creates a magnetic field
Switching off the current removes the magnetic field
The magnetic field produced by an electric current — passing current through a wire creates a field around it; the basis of electromagnets

definition: A coil of wire that, when carrying an electric current, produces a magnetic field similar to that of a bar magnet. The field is strongest inside the coil.
clues: This is a coil of wire that acts as a magnet
It produces a field similar to a bar magnet when current flows
The field is strongest inside it
A coil of wire carrying current — produces a magnetic field like a bar magnet; adding an iron core makes it an electromagnet

definition: A solenoid with an iron core inside it. The iron core becomes an induced magnet, greatly increasing the strength of the magnetic field. The magnetism can be switched on and off.
clues: This is a type of magnet that can be switched on and off
It is a solenoid with an iron core
The core becomes a magnet when current flows
A solenoid with a soft iron core — current induces magnetism in the core, greatly boosting the field; used in cranes, circuit breakers and bells

definition: A rule used to determine the direction of the magnetic field around a current-carrying wire. Point the thumb in the direction of conventional current; the curled fingers show the direction of the field.
clues: This is a rule used in electromagnetism
It involves the thumb and fingers of the right hand
It gives the direction of the magnetic field around a wire
Thumb points in direction of conventional current; curled fingers show the direction of the magnetic field circling the wire

definition: The force experienced by a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field. The force is perpendicular to both the current and the magnetic field.
clues: This is a phenomenon in electromagnetism
A current-carrying wire in a magnetic field experiences a force
The force is perpendicular to both current and field
When a current flows through a wire in a magnetic field, a force acts on the wire — the basis of electric motors

definition: A rule used to find the direction of the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field. The thumb points in the direction of motion (force), the index finger in the direction of the field, and the middle finger in the direction of conventional current.
clues: This is a rule used in the motor effect
It uses three fingers of the left hand
The thumb gives the direction of force
Left hand: thumb = force/motion, index finger = field direction, middle finger = conventional current direction

definition: The force acting on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field. Calculated using: F = BIL, where B is magnetic flux density, I is current, and L is length of conductor in the field.
clues: This is a force experienced by a wire in a magnetic field
It is calculated using F = BIL
It increases with stronger field, more current or longer wire
F = BIL — the force on a wire carrying current in a magnetic field; increased by raising field strength, current or conductor length

definition: A measure of the strength of a magnetic field. Symbol B, measured in tesla (T). A stronger magnetic field has a greater magnetic flux density.
clues: This is a measure of magnetic field strength
Its symbol is B
It is measured in tesla
The strength of a magnetic field — symbol B, measured in tesla (T); used in F = BIL and the transformer equations

definition: The SI unit of magnetic flux density (T). A field of 1 tesla exerts a force of 1 newton on a 1-metre conductor carrying a current of 1 ampere.
clues: This is a unit of measurement in physics
It is the unit of magnetic flux density
1 of these produces a force of 1 N on a 1 m wire carrying 1 A
The SI unit of magnetic field strength — 1 T = 1 N/(A·m); named after Nikola Tesla

definition: A device that uses the motor effect to convert electrical energy into rotational kinetic energy. A current-carrying coil in a magnetic field experiences forces that cause it to rotate.
clues: This is a device that converts electrical energy
It produces rotational movement
It uses the motor effect
A device using the force on a current in a magnetic field to produce rotation — converts electrical energy to kinetic energy; used in fans, drills and EVs

definition: A device in a DC electric motor that reverses the direction of the current through the coil every half turn, ensuring the coil continues to rotate in the same direction.
clues: This is a component of a DC electric motor
It reverses the current direction every half turn
It keeps the coil spinning in the same direction
A rotating contact in a DC motor — reverses the current through the coil every 180° so the torque always acts in the same rotational direction

definition: The process by which a changing magnetic field induces (generates) a potential difference (voltage) in a conductor. The basis of generators and transformers.
clues: This is a fundamental process in physics
A changing magnetic field causes a voltage
It is the basis of generators and transformers
A conductor experiencing a changing magnetic flux has a potential difference induced in it — moving a magnet into a coil generates a voltage

definition: The voltage generated in a conductor when there is a change in the magnetic field through it or when the conductor moves through a magnetic field.
clues: This is a voltage that is generated, not from a battery
It is produced by a changing magnetic field
Moving a conductor through a magnetic field produces this
The EMF generated by electromagnetic induction — can be increased by using a stronger field, more coil turns, or moving faster

definition: The induced potential difference is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux. A faster change or stronger field induces a greater potential difference.
clues: This is a law in electromagnetism
It relates induced voltage to the rate of change of magnetic flux
A faster change produces a greater voltage
The induced EMF is proportional to the rate at which magnetic flux changes — faster movement or stronger field = larger induced voltage

definition: The direction of an induced current is always such that it opposes the change that caused it. This is consistent with the conservation of energy.
clues: This is a law in electromagnetism
The induced current opposes the change that caused it
It is consistent with conservation of energy
The induced current always acts to oppose the change in flux that created it — you must do work against this opposition, which converts to electrical energy

definition: A device that converts kinetic energy into electrical energy using electromagnetic induction. A coil rotating in a magnetic field generates an alternating current (AC).
clues: This is a device that produces electricity
It uses electromagnetic induction
A rotating coil in a magnetic field generates AC
Converts kinetic energy to electrical energy — a coil rotates in a magnetic field, inducing an alternating current; used in power stations

definition: An electric current that repeatedly reverses direction. Generated by rotating coils in magnetic fields. The UK mains supply is AC at 50 Hz and 230 V.
clues: This is a type of electric current
It repeatedly reverses direction
The UK mains supply is this type at 50 Hz
Current that periodically changes direction — generated by rotating coils; UK mains is 230 V at 50 Hz

definition: An electric current that flows in one direction only. Produced by batteries and solar cells.
clues: This is a type of electric current
It flows in one direction only
Batteries produce this type
Current flowing in a single direction — produced by batteries and solar cells; must be converted to AC for efficient long-distance transmission

definition: A device that uses electromagnetic induction to change the voltage of an alternating current. Consists of two coils (primary and secondary) wound around an iron core.
clues: This is a device that changes voltage
It uses electromagnetic induction
It has two coils wound around an iron core
Two coils around an iron core — AC in the primary coil induces a changing flux, which induces a voltage in the secondary coil

definition: The input coil of a transformer, connected to the supply voltage. The alternating current in this coil creates a changing magnetic field in the iron core.
clues: This is a component of a transformer
It is connected to the input voltage
The AC in it creates a changing magnetic field
The input coil of a transformer — AC flows through it creating a changing magnetic flux in the iron core, which induces a voltage in the secondary coil

definition: The output coil of a transformer. The changing magnetic field from the primary coil induces a potential difference in this coil.
clues: This is a component of a transformer
It is connected to the output
The changing flux from the primary induces a voltage in it
The output coil of a transformer — the changing flux from the primary induces an EMF here; more turns = higher output voltage

definition: A transformer where the secondary coil has more turns than the primary coil, resulting in a higher output voltage than input voltage.
clues: This is a type of transformer
It increases voltage
The secondary coil has more turns than the primary
A transformer with more turns on the secondary than the primary — increases voltage; used at power stations before grid transmission

definition: A transformer where the secondary coil has fewer turns than the primary coil, resulting in a lower output voltage than input voltage.
clues: This is a type of transformer
It decreases voltage
The secondary coil has fewer turns than the primary
A transformer with fewer turns on the secondary than the primary — decreases voltage; used before electricity enters homes

definition: Relates the voltages and number of turns in a transformer: Vp/Vs = np/ns, where Vp and Vs are primary and secondary voltages, and np and ns are the number of turns in each coil.
clues: This is an equation used with transformers
It links voltages and the number of turns in both coils
Vp/Vs = np/ns
The turns ratio equals the voltage ratio — Vp/Vs = np/ns; used to calculate unknown voltages or turns in transformer problems

definition: The network of pylons, cables, and transformers that distributes electricity from power stations to homes and businesses across the country.
clues: This is a system for distributing electricity nationwide
It uses pylons, cables and transformers
It transmits at high voltage to reduce energy loss
The network distributing electricity across the country — high voltage transmission minimises power loss in cables; step-down transformers reduce voltage for consumers

definition: Energy lost as heat in the cables of the National Grid due to the resistance of the wires. Calculated using P = I²R. Using high voltage and low current reduces power loss.
clues: This is a problem in electrical transmission
It is caused by resistance in cables
High voltage and low current reduces it
Heat dissipated in cables — P = I²R; transmitting at high voltage reduces current, which dramatically reduces power lost as heat
